title: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure at the point of publication. A fabricated video carried the branding of a news outlet that had nothing to do with it, and the false claim travelled under that outlet's name rather than the fabricator's. The impersonation was the delivery mechanism, not an incidental detail: the invented logo lent the claim an authority the posting account did not have.

The account that posted it had no followers, which is the signature of a disposable distribution node rather than an audience. Reach came from the platform's recommendation and sharing surfaces, not from any following the account had built. Catching this before it spread would have required either the platform or the outlet to detect the misuse of a trademark and a brand identity at upload time, and the outlet only learned of it when outside researchers flagged it.

What is not established is who exactly operated the accounts, and the attribution to a named network rests on the reporting of researchers and one outlet rather than on any finding presented here. The claim in the video is false, but the summary does not establish the intent of any individual poster, and the removal was a platform trademark decision, not an adjudication of the disinformation campaign.

reports.title: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake

summary:
A Russian disinformation network known as Storm-1679 or Matryoshka has been spreading fake videos on social media ahead of the 2026 midterms. One video, falsely branded with a Mother Jones logo, claimed the Democratic National Committee paid $259 million to CNN chief Mark Thompson to promote gender transition among children. It was posted by an X account called роман, which appeared to be a bot with no followers, and drew 155,000 views within a day, plus another 50,000 views on a second account. The campaign has also used deepfakes of celebrities like Sarah Jessica Parker and Julia Roberts.

Mother Jones complained to X after being alerted by researchers at @antibot4navalny, and X removed the post for violating its trademark policy. The article says the operation has not yet gained major reach, but warns that the Trump administration has closed FBI, intelligence, and State Department units that once tracked Russian disinformation, leaving the US more exposed to foreign interference in the midterms.
